Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Amit Mahajan

The present application is filed seeking regular bail in FIR No.87/2020 dated 03.02.2020,
registered at Police Station Moti Nagar for offence under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
Chargesheet in the present case was filed under Sections 376/302 of the IPC.
2. The FIR was registered pursuant to a PCR call regarding a murder of a lady.
The deceased was identified by her son.
The statement of the victim's son was recorded, who stated that the applicant used to visit their house to meet his mother and also used to stay with her.

He also stated that two days prior to the incident, the victim had gone with the applicant and on 03.02.2020 when he reached his home for changing his shoes, he found the door of the house half opened and found his mother lying on the floor with blood oozing out from her nose and mouth.

During the course of the investigation, the police examined the landlord, who stated that the victim was residing in the property with her son and the applicant used to meet the victim regularly.
He further stated that on the night of 02.02.2020 around 9:00 PM he had seen the applicant at the house.
4. It is alleged that the applicant during interrogation confessed that he committed the murder.
5. At this stage, there is substantial evidence against the applicant, which prima facie indicates towards his involvement in the crime.

sentences.text: 6. It is further pointed out that the blood of the deceased was detected on the jacket belonging to the applicant which was also found lying at the scene of crime.
As per the FSL report, the blood of the applicant was also detected in the clothes which the deceased was wearing.

7. The applicant has been charged for the offence under Section 302 of the IPC for which the minimum punishment is upto life, The Hon'ble Apex Court, recently, in the case of X v. State of Rajasthan & Anr. : 2024 INSC 909, in a challenge to the order passed by the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan whereby the bail application filed by the accused was allowed observed as under:
"14.

sentences.text: Ordinarily in serious offences like rape, murder, dacoity, etc., once the trial commences and the prosecution starts examining its witnesses, the Court be it the Trial Court or the High Court should be loath in entertaining the bail application of the accused.

15. Over a period of time, we have noticed two things, i.e., (i) either bail is granted after the charge is framed and just before the victim is to be examined by the prosecution before This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 27/06/2025 at 23:37:50 the trial court, or (ii) bail is granted once the recording of the oral evidence of the victim is complete by looking into some discrepancies here or there in the deposition and thereby testing the credibility of the victim.
16. We are of the view that the aforesaid is not a correct practice that the Courts below should adopt.
Once the trial commences, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion which may either result in the conviction of the accused or acquittal of the accused.

The moment the High Court exercises its discretion in favour of the accused and orders release of the accused on bail by looking into the deposition of the victim, it will have its own impact on the pending trial when it comes to appreciating the oral evidence of the victim.

It is only in the event if the trial gets unduly delayed and that too for no fault on the part of the accused, the Court may be justified in ordering his release on bail on the ground that right of the accused to have a speedy trial has been infringed."
8.
It is pointed out that 16 out of 22 witnesses have already been examined and the trial is at its fag end.
9. In view of the aforesaid, no case is made out for grant of bail to the applicant.
